Below is the behavioral history of a student across several economic games played with classmates. Use this to predict their behavior in the Tolerance for Inequality task described at the end.


**Game 1 — Competition Task (Slider Task)**
Students completed a slider task (centering sliders on a 0–100 scale) then chose how to be paid:
  • Option A (safe): 0.20 credits per correct slider regardless of partner
  • Option B (competitive): 0.50 credits per correct slider only if they outperformed their partner; 0 otherwise
Choice: Option A (safe/fixed)
Performance: 25 out of 48 sliders centered correctly

**Game 2 — Mutual Aid Game (4 rounds)**
Each round, students received 1 credit and chose how much to send to a partner (0–1, in steps of 0.1).
Whatever was sent was doubled before reaching the partner.
  Round 1: sent 0.3 credits
  Round 2: sent 0.3 credits
  Round 3: sent 0.4 credits
  Round 4: sent 0.2 credits

**Game 3 — Coordination Game (4 rounds)**
Each round, students chose Option A or Option B when paired with a partner:
  • Option A: always earns 3 credits (safe)
  • Option B: earns 5 credits only if partner also chose B; earns 0 otherwise (risky)
  Round 1: chose A
  Round 2: chose A
  Round 3: chose A
  Round 4: chose A

**Game 4 — Guessing Game / Beauty Contest (4 rounds)**
Each round, students guessed a number from 0–100. The student closest to 1/2 of the group average won 6 credits.
  Round 1: guessed 46
  Round 2: guessed 8 (won)
  Round 3: guessed 17
  Round 4: guessed 4 (won)

**Game 5 — Individual Decision Games (5 tasks)**
  5a. Time Preferences: allocated 3 credit(s) to next month (receives 6 credits next month) and 2 credit(s) today
  5b. Risk Task (BRET): opened 4 out of 10 boxes (one box hid a bomb; opening it meant earning nothing)
  5c. Dictator Game: out of 10 credits, gave 2 to another student and kept 8
  5d. Moral Preferences (5 decisions — for each, chose between personal earnings or donation to UNICEF):
       Decision 1 (self=2 credits vs UNICEF): donated to UNICEF (10 credits)
       Decision 2 (self=4 credits vs UNICEF): kept 4 credits for themselves
       Decision 3 (self=6 credits vs UNICEF): kept 6 credits for themselves
       Decision 4 (self=8 credits vs UNICEF): kept 8 credits for themselves
       Decision 5 (self=10 credits vs UNICEF): kept 10 credits for themselves
  5e. Lying Game: privately rolled a die and reported 6 (higher reports = higher payment; truthful reporting cannot be verified)

**Game 8 — Trust Game**
Each student played both roles simultaneously:
  • As Sender: receives 5 credits, decides how much to send (0–5, steps of 0.5). Amount sent is tripled.
  • As Receiver: decides how much to return to the sender.
  Sent (as Sender): 1.5 credits
  Returned (as Receiver): 3.0 credits
